item.title: Prime Minister w/ Q&A | Additional Films and Guests — Wed Oct 21, 7:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
This gripping documentary chronicles Jacinda Ardern navigating unprecedented national tragedies, a volcanic eruption, and a global pandemic as New Zealand’s youngest female leader. By balancing immense political pressure with first-time motherhood, she redefines global leadership through an empathetic yet resolute approach. Packed with raw audio diaries and candid footage, this film delivers a powerful, inspiring portrait of a woman who proved that vulnerability and unyielding strength can rewrite the rules of power. [101 min; documentary; English]
A Q&A will follow the screening.
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: Yonder Mountain String Band — Wed Oct 21, 7:00 PM — Buskirk-Chumley Theater
item.description:
Grammy-nominated Yonder Mountain String Band https://www.yondermountain.com/ set the tone for a new way forward in acoustic music, carrying bluegrass into rooms and conversations it had never reached before.
Nearly three decades later, that same spirit still guides them, alive and present on Good As True (2026), the band’s 12th studio album, arriving March 27th, 2026. The record captures Yonder in full stride. It’s unguarded and in motion, preserving the spark of musicians playing in real time and leaning into everything they have learned along the way.
Good As True (2026) digs into communication, the conversations that carry us forward and the ones that fall apart. The things we say, the things we mean, and what gets lost in between.

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Thu Oct 22 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Thu Oct 22 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Thu Oct 22 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.description:

item.title: Affirmation Thursday — Thu Oct 22, 11:45 AM — Indiana Memorial Union – Table 2
item.description:
Affirmation Thursday is a tabling event at the Indiana Memorial Union designed to support students' mental well-being during their first months of the semester. Our organization will hand out positive affirmations to passing students and provide a space for them to write down their thoughts and feelings about their first month of school. The event aims to foster a sense of belonging and encourage students to pause, reflect, and practice self-kindness during a busy and often stressful transition. Participation is free and open to all students, and no sign-up is required. Materials will include affirmation cards, writing supplies, and a table display.
Hosted by: Black Men Evolve
Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12910866
Source: IU beINvolved Student Orgs

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Tue Oct 27 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Tue Oct 27 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery.
